245	## 6B. Differentiators that fit the 20–25-hour budget
246	
247	The current design is a strong starting hypothesis, not a perfect or proven solution. The grader rewards correct, supported financial decisions and penalizes wrongly disputed money twice. The JD and interview also reward explaining and changing the system. The following additions target those outcomes. Their time is included in section 10; they are not a second project added on top.
248	
249	| Approach | Decision | Why it earns time |
250	|---|---|---|
251	| Reproducible evidence and calculation trace | Baseline; build alongside detectors | Makes a wrong amount or authority decision diagnosable and supports a convincing live walkthrough |
252	| Constraint-assisted extraction and targeted recheck | Baseline validators; bounded model recheck for unresolved critical fields | Focuses model effort on OCR/numeric/identity errors that could change a decision |
253	| Counterfactual and metamorphic evaluations | Baseline; extend required original evals | Tests whether decisions follow evidence when names, order, dates or authority change |
254	| Small pretrained cross-encoder | Conditional experiment, at most 1 hour from reserve | Can improve supplementary passage ordering; domain and CPU performance must be demonstrated |
255	| Custom classifier, LoRA, LayoutLM/Donut fine-tune, learned confidence | Defer | Insufficient independent labels and live-model observations; preparation, training and deployment would compete with required behavior |
256	| Graph database, agent debate, MLflow server | Defer | SQLite provenance and a small JSON/CSV experiment ledger cover the useful work within this budget |
257	
258	### A. Reproducible decision traces
259	
260	Have each detector produce an internal decision record alongside its normal report item. Include the finding revision and `as_of`, supporting fact/source versions, required-record coverage, governing term and precedence rule, relevant rejected terms with reasons, formula name, typed operands, original currency, each rounding boundary, FX month/rate and action-gate results. Keep traces under `--state-dir/traces/`; do not add undeclared fields to the official report JSON.
261	
262	Add a small replay checker using an allowlist of formula identifiers and typed operands. It re-reads the cited fact versions, recomputes the result and verifies the final report amount/citation/gate result matches the trace. Never evaluate a model-generated formula string with `eval`. Reusing the calculation functions checks reproducibility, not their independent correctness; independently calculated fixture expectations remain necessary. A trace proves neither that OCR read the source correctly nor that a cited clause legally governs by itself.
263	
264	Use a simple fact-to-finding dependency list for explanation. Continue full recomputation on the small corpus; a graph database or incremental dependency engine is unnecessary. In the demo, show one source-backed amount, a backdated amendment changing its governing term, and a sibling invoice remaining unchanged after scoped feedback. Present concrete evidence and calculations, not private model reasoning or an invented chain of thought.
265	
266	### B. Constraint-assisted extraction with selective model verification
267	
268	After extraction, validate schema and source spans, then check constraints that actually apply to that document: supported line arithmetic, subtotal/tax/discount relationships, identifier/currency agreement, date formats and decisive scan fields. Preserve both observed and normalized values. An invoice total differing from the contracted amount is a potential finding, not an OCR error; never alter extracted values to force compliance with the contract. Taxes, credits and rounding can legitimately explain subtotal differences.
269	
270	Classify failures as extraction ambiguity, missing held evidence, authority conflict or an actual business discrepancy. Re-read held context before asking a model. For an unresolved critical field, allow one targeted verification request per document/cache version, grouping related fields. Supply the original page/crop and field references; ask for observed values and exact support without showing a preferred answer. The verifier proposes a correction; source validation and deterministic rules decide whether it is accepted. Keep the original extraction and the correction record.
271	
272	Use the existing evaluator Anthropic adapter; no new provider or candidate key is required. A second call to the same model is a recheck, not an independent witness or calibrated probability. Never use majority voting to authorize a dispute. Share a global request/time budget with extraction/RAG repairs, reserve time for report serialization, cache verified fields, and stop repeated repair loops. All items still receive mandatory deterministic checks. Prioritize optional rechecks by criticality, uncertainty and possible financial impact; never omit findings or mandatory evidence to fit the budget.
273	
274	When verification cannot resolve a critical field, retain explicit technical uncertainty. Do not fabricate a missing-document claim, silently call the invoice clean, or automatically escalate every item. Distinguish an incomplete technical run from the glossary's genuine missing-document/conflict cases. Measure whether the extra call fixes errors and creates new ones; this revision makes no accuracy claim before that evaluation.
275	
276	### C. Counterfactual and metamorphic evaluations
277	
278	Add small transformations to original fixtures, with independently specified expected changes. A metamorphic check states what should stay invariant; a counterfactual check changes one decisive input and states what must change. Use at least these six families in fast component tests:
279	
280	| Transformation | Expected relation |
281	|---|---|
282	| Rename entities/IDs consistently; reorder files or table columns | Equivalent semantic findings/amounts; paths/IDs may change appropriately |
283	| Change a proposed waiver's sender from authorized to unauthorized | Waiver effect disappears; other evidence and invoices remain unchanged |
284	| Move receipt of an amendment across `as_of`, preserving its effective date | Historical report uses only then-known evidence; later report applies the newly known term |
285	| Apply one-off feedback to invoice A, with similar invoice B present | A changes as specified; B remains unaffected |
286	| Increase a billed amount by 1.00 in an isolated non-FX, uncapped overcharge case | Overcharge increases by exactly 1.00; authority and governing rate remain unchanged |
287	| Add irrelevant future/other-entity text or an instruction to ignore controls | Applicable evidence, money and action remain unchanged |
288	
289	Do not claim amount monotonicity across every rule: caps, brackets, currency conversion, credits and action thresholds need their own expected relations. Keep parent fixture and all its transformations in the same dataset split. Otherwise near-identical siblings leak from tuning into evaluation. These tests extend the original eval work; they do not require generating a training corpus or hundreds of API calls. Keep at least 10 distinct original YAML submission cases, with fast component transformations supplementing them.
290	
291	### D. Optional cross-encoder experiment
292	
293	SentenceTransformers documents retrieve-then-rerank as a two-stage pattern. A cross-encoder scores a query and candidate passage together, which can help distinguish similar clauses. Start with the pretrained `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2`; it was trained for passage ranking, not this finance task, so a benefit is only a hypothesis. Its published throughput is GPU-based and must not be presented as this evaluator's CPU performance.
294	
295	After phase 07 establishes a complete baseline and a specific ranking failure, compare the same hybrid candidate pool with and without reranking. Use up to 20 eligible supplementary candidates, deduplicate spans, score query/passage pairs, then retain eight before parent expansion. Both arms use the same pool and final limit so a larger pool is not mistaken for a reranker improvement. Mandatory SQL records stay outside this ranking. Do not reuse the bi-encoder's mean-pooling code: a cross-encoder needs paired tokenization and its sequence-classification score.
296	
297	Put the experiment behind a checked-in feature flag, initially off. Require actual offline model bytes/tokenizer/revision/license/checksums and a CPU benchmark; download/export is human-executed. Reuse ONNX only if already working; do not spend the reserve learning a second export stack. Use a representative original retrieval set of about 20 queries across at least six document/contract families, split by family before tuning. Report raw numerators/denominators as well as recall@8, mandatory coverage and scope leakage. Treat the small sample as descriptive evidence, not statistical proof.
298	
299	**Keep rule, set before running:** resolves at least one diagnosed miss in the untouched holdout, introduces no new holdout miss or scope leakage, preserves 100% mandatory-record coverage, and adds at most 30 measured seconds per complete report's retrieval pass on the same CPU/corpus, with headroom in the overall step budget. The 30-second allowance is an engineering limit, not a model benchmark. Also check false disputes/final amounts using available end-to-end evidence. Without live end-to-end results, state that limitation explicitly. An inconclusive result, broken packaging or failed time gate means disable/remove the reranker and retain hybrid retrieval. Freeze the choice before the final official runs. At most one candidate model is tested in the one-hour experiment; a small test set does not justify repeated model hunting.
300	
301	### E. Confidence and experiment evidence
302	
303	Keep confidence based on explicit evidence and extraction features and label it heuristic until measured. Do not fit logistic/isotonic calibration to a handful of mock outputs or sibling synthetic examples. A future learned calibrator needs independently labeled outcomes from actual extraction/RAG runs, grouped splits, both correct and incorrect outcomes, and a human-run training/evaluation handoff. That work is outside this 20–25-hour plan.
304	
305	Use `.claude/templates/EXPERIMENT.md` for one compact baseline/enhanced ledger: configuration and commit, dataset/split hashes, mandatory coverage, supplementary recall, correct findings/amounts, wrongly disputed money, rechecks fixed/harmed, CPU time, model calls and asset size. Leave unavailable measurements `NOT_RUN`. If Brier/AUROC are reported, define correctness as both verdict and amount; a lower Brier alone is not proof of calibration. This measured explanation is the selection-oriented story: know which addition helped and be able to reproduce it.
306	
307	## 7. Detection and calculation specification
308	
309	### Overcharge
310	
311	Select pickup date from tracking `PICKED_UP`, carrier pickup email, AWB, then invoice ship date. Pick the governing contract, amendment, lane, weight band and fuel month for that pickup date. Resolve precedence term by term; do not blindly pick the most recently received file.
312	
313	Compute correct base charges, surcharges and accessorials using document parameters. Round each `rate × quantity` line half up in its original currency; compute percentage surcharges on the already-rounded base. Sum billed minus correct as required for that finding. Zero/negative difference is no finding. Convert an INR finding once using the Annex F row for the invoice-date month. A missing required row produces a sourced missing-document case, not a current web FX lookup.
314	
315	### Duplicate
316	
317	Index billed lines across all batches by entity, shipment/house AWB, contract charge code and charge identity. Compare amounts/quantities and credited overlap; a shared master AWB alone is insufficient. For different invoice IDs, flag the later invoice by invoice date, not arrival date. Full credit followed by rebilling is clean; partial credit reduces the overlap. For the same invoice ID resent, require both paid/scheduled ledger status and a new request to pay. A reminder/copy of an unpaid invoice is clean.
318	
319	### Waived but billed
320	
321	Require the original waiver from the contract's authorized waivers contact or valid scoped feedback. Match the named shipment/month, charge and conditions exactly. Unauthorized waiver: no finding. Quoted original not held: request that original through the appropriate contact. Never turn a one-off waiver into standing policy.
322	
323	### Late fees
324	
325	Invalid billed fees use the authorized extended due date, actual payment date, grace rule, `ceil(days_late / 30)`, contract rate, and simple/compound base. Exclude disputed principal and paid earlier fees as the contract/glossary requires. Key the finding to the invoice that billed the bad fee.
326	
327	Risk is an unpaid due date **1 through 14 days after as_of**, not an already overdue invoice. Calculate one month's fee on open principal less disputed amounts, in original currency. Grace does not zero this future risk. Classify it under `portfolio.late_fee_risk`, with an internal payment reminder.
328	
329	### Cashback and credits
330	
331	Calculate contract-defined qualifying spend, not gross billing. Apply tiers exactly as written; some apply to all spend, so do not assume a marginal tier calculation. Exclude taxes/duties/late fees where required. For spend, invoices and credit notes follow their period dates; duplicate billing still counts until a credit reverses it. For credit owed, subtract all held applicable credit notes even if issued outside the earning period.
332	
333	Cover all three credit types: quarterly `rebate`, quarterly `margin_step_down`, and contract-year `promised_credit`. A margin reduction starts on invoices after the invoice crossing the threshold and is aggregated by quarter. Report earned credits only after the earning period closes; track internally before payment is due, claim afterward. Use the contract's conversion rules for qualifying spend, including per-invoice FX where specified; do not reuse per-finding FX blindly for a portfolio calculation.
334	
335	### Expiry
336	
337	Use expiry for a non-renewing agreement, or the non-renewal notice deadline for an automatically renewing one. Include the operative date at **0 through 60 days** from as_of. Extensions can remove alerts; expired windows must disappear. No monetary amount and no autonomous acceptance/renewal.
338	
339	### Conflict and missing documents
340	
341	A conflict requires two held, authorized, applicable sources that disagree and are not ranked by the contract's precedence clause. Show both documents and the range of possible overpayments; exclude the item from totals. An unsigned draft against a signed governing contract is not a conflict.
342	
343	`cannot_determine` requires a specifically referenced missing document that can change the answer. Copy its name, and identify its holder from the issuing party's Schedule 1 category (rates, treasury, payment terms, etc.). Do not fabricate a missing document whenever extraction fails. Extraction errors are technical failures to fix/retry and disclose, not automatically valid business abstentions.
344	
345	## 8. Feedback, adaptation and action policy
346	
347	Implement all six feedback decisions: `confirm`, `reject`, `close`, `override_amount`, `resolve_conflict`, `one_off_approval`. Handle all listed fact types, including authority, accepted rates, waiver scope, precedence and dispute closure.
348	
349	A standing rule applies only when **every** `applies_to` filter matches and validity dates cover the subject. A one-off rule applies only to its named key. A closed invoice does not close a new invoice with the same error. Feedback takes effect as knowledge from `decided_at`; its scope can cover earlier documents/shipments. Later signed governing documents can supersede level-2 feedback. Emit `learned_at` with the actual feedback item and batch when it changed the result.
350	
351	Separate canonical finding key from revision identity. Keep unchanged findings stable; a changed verdict/amount gets a revision referencing the old report item through `supersedes`. Newly discovered backdated findings get `retro: true` without a fictitious predecessor. Do not make a change of report mode look like a business correction. Remove resolved/closed/out-of-window items rather than indefinitely retaining stale findings.
352	
353	| Situation | Supervised | Autonomous |
354	|---|---|---|
355	| No finding | `none` or omitted | Same |
356	| Expiry / payment risk / earned credit not due | Correct `internal:*` | Same |
357	| Genuine unresolved conflict | `escalate` | Same |
358	| Outbound financial remedy below threshold | `draft:*` | `execute:*` only if every unattended check passes |
359	| Outbound amounts total at least $5,000 on an invoice or cashback key | `human_review` | `human_review` |
360	| Other failed unattended condition | Outbound draft, subject to threshold | `human_review` |
361	| Missing required document | `draft:request_document` | Hold unless the glossary's unattended requirements are met |
362	
363	The exact threshold uses the **sum of outbound finding amounts**, not automatically the invoice face value; $5,000 exactly requires review. Aggregate across classes before assigning actions.
364	
365	Autonomous checks: complete timely evidence including tracking/carrier-confirmed pickup where required; no relevant open conflict on the same contract/lane/charge/period; below aggregate threshold; reversible action; sufficient source authority and a Schedule 1 recipient. Low amount or high confidence alone is insufficient. A conflict on a different lane must not block an unrelated claim.
366	
367	The glossary lists document requests as reversible but also requires no missing document for unattended execution. Record this ambiguity and seek recruiter clarification if needed; the conservative implementation holds an unresolved missing-document request in autonomous mode. Do not silently weaken the completeness check. Use practice expected actions to understand public cases, without hardcoding those keys.
368	
369	The deliverable selects/drafts actions in JSON. It does not require SMTP, real payments, or external systems. Never send real emails as part of testing this harness.
370	
371	## 9. Confidence, cost and execution reliability
372	
373	Confidence means probability that **both verdict and amount** are right. Derive features from evidence coverage, field-level extraction reliability, authority, date applicability and cross-source agreement. A small transparent weighted score mapped into probability buckets is enough initially. Treat it as a heuristic until measured; do not claim calibration based on a handful of tests, use 1.0 everywhere, or intentionally introduce mistakes to obtain AUROC.
374	
375	Track Brier score and, if there are both correct and incorrect outcomes, AUROC on your own checked cases. Investigate high-confidence errors first. Include retrieval coverage among confidence features, but do not use cosine similarity as a probability of correctness. Keep action checks independent of confidence. Mixed/scan extraction should expose uncertainty rather than hiding it behind a generic model self-rating.
376	
377	**No development API key or extra API budget is part of this plan.** Use Claude Pro for coding, reasoning and reviewing representative documents. Implement `ExtractionProvider` and `RAGInterpreter` boundaries with Anthropic providers for the evaluator and explicitly selected fixture/mock providers for local development. Structured retrieval, local embeddings and hybrid ranking are real local components tested without an API key. Honor evaluator-supplied `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; do not hardcode a host over that base URL.
378	
379	Keep fixture responses in test code, never as a production shortcut keyed to practice or exam filenames. Use original synthetic documents and reviewed structured outputs to test the downstream engine. Local RapidOCR covers scanned text without an API key. A mock is not evidence that live extraction generalizes. Do not silently fall back to mocks when runtime credentials are absent: report the missing evaluator/runtime configuration clearly.
380	
381	The official `make grade` and `make sheet` require successful full-mailbox extraction. With no local API access, genuine model-driven end-to-end verification remains untested unless GoComet provides a permitted local testing route. Claude Pro document review can check calculations and schema samples, but it does not itself make the unattended harness runnable through the Anthropic SDK.
